## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)

*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*

The *Bahujanahita Sutta* ("For the Welfare of the People", Iti 84) is a discourse found in the third section of the *Itivuttaka* (It 3.35, PTS It 78) [SuttaCentral]. The text expounds upon three types of persons who appear in the world for the welfare, benefit, and happiness of the people [SuttaCentral].

In comparative literature, SuttaCentral identifies a full parallel preserved in the Chinese Buddhist canon at T 765.138 [SuttaCentral]. SuttaCentral catalogs eighteen translations in sixteen languages, including an English translation by Bhikkhu Sujato [SuttaCentral].

Automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse, with 368 matching passages detected across 59 other canonical and paracanonical texts [DharmaNexus]. Strong phraseological and passage sharing occurs particularly with the Aṅguttara Nikāya—notably the *Ekakanipāta* (AN 1), *Catukkanipāta* (AN 4), *Dukanipāta* (AN 2), *Navakanipāta* (AN 9), and *Tikanipāta* (AN 3)—alongside the Abhidhamma's *Tikapuggalapaññatti* (Pp 2.3), the Dīgha Nikāya (*Ambaṭṭha Sutta*, DN 3, and *Saṅgīti Sutta*, DN 33), the Vinaya *Mahākhandhaka* (Kd 1), and within the *Itivuttaka* itself (*Saṁghasāmaggī Sutta*, Iti 19) [DharmaNexus].

*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
